housing.title: Gear housing
housing.what: pos. 5: 1 × Gear housing (own part, milled, EN AW-6082 T6)
housing.why: Carries everything: rail, both bearings of the pinion shaft and the gearbox. Milled from one block of the standard machining alloy.
values: length 200 mm (grew from 164 mm: brake and encoder bracket on both sides, kept symmetric)
wall 7 mm - the M3 cover screws sit on the wall centre line
top plate 7 mm (thinned on 11 Nov; the bearings sit in a boss above it)
at least 1.5 mm of material around every hole, checked for every own part

hood.title: Drive hood
hood.what: pos. 4: 1 × Drive hood (own part, milled, EN AW-6082 T6)
hood.why: Closes the drive train and carries the robot adapter. The adapter screws go into wire thread inserts, because a thread in aluminium that is opened again and again wears out.
values: pos. 40: 4 × Wire thread insert HELICOIL plus M4 x 1.5 d, hood seat for the adapter screws (Boellhoff, 1.4301)

cover.title: Bottom cover
cover.what: pos. 1: 1 × Bottom cover (own part, cut + milled, EN AW-6082 T6)
cover.why: Closes the housing from below; the two slots let the jaw holders through. Brush strips in the slots keep oil and dirt from the oily parts out of the rail.
values: pos. 42: 2 × Brush seal strip along the two holder slots in the cover (oily parts) (e.g. Mink LKB, cut to length, PA / steel)
ISO 10642 countersunk screws: the underside stays flat

window.title: Cable window and gland
window.what: pos. 2: 1 × Cable window plate (own part, cut, EN AW-6082 T6); pos. 12: 1 × Cable gland SKINTOP STR-M 16x1.5 (Lapp, PA)
window.why: The motor, brake and encoder cable leaves the hood through a sealed gland in the side window.
values: SKINTOP M16 × 1.5: strain relief and seal in one part

adapter.title: Robot adapter ISO 9409-1-40-4-M6
adapter.what: pos. 9: 1 × Robot adapter ISO 9409-1-40-4-M6 (own part, turned, EN AW-6082 T6)
adapter.why: The standard flange of the ABB IRB 1300: any tool with this flange fits, and the dowel pin fixes the angle so the gripper always sits the same way on the robot.
values: Ø 76 mm, 10 mm thick, spigot Ø 25 × 4.5 mm
pos. 43: 4 × ISO 4762 M6x10, 8.8, adapter to the robot flange (heads in the counterbores) (standard part, steel 8.8)
pos. 44: 1 × Dowel pin ISO 8734 6 m6 x 14, ISO 9409 orientation (pressed into the adapter) (standard part, steel)
to the hood: 4 × ISO 10642 M4x16 countersunk from the top, into wire thread inserts
gripper + part 3.55 kg of the robot's 7 kg

motor.title: Stepper motor
motor.what: pos. 23: 1 × Stepper motor ST4118S1404-B, long B shaft through brake and encoder (Nanotec)
motor.why: The motor current sets the grip force: limit the current and the gripper can never squeeze harder than intended. Closed loop: the encoder tells the controller where the jaws are.
values: holding torque 0.2 N·m (NEMA 17)
available at the jaws at full current, all losses: 60.5 N per jaw against the setpoint 44.5 N
the current limit is set to the setpoint

brake.title: Permanent-magnet brake
brake.what: pos. 17: 1 × Permanent-magnet brake BRAKE-BKE-0,4-5,0, 24 V, zero backlash, on a 3 mm adapter plate (Nanotec)
brake.why: On a power failure the grip force would be gone in about 2 ms and the part would fall. The brake holds the drive; it must be free of play, because every degree of play at the motor shaft releases grip force.
values: holding torque 0.4 N·m
allowed play at the motor shaft: 1.12° before nothing is left against the weight
the spring brake BWA we had first allowed up to 2° → replaced by this zero-backlash brake (review 21 Nov)
brake-first shutdown: the brake closes before the motor current drops (MuJoCo, power_fail.py)

encoder.title: Encoder
encoder.what: pos. 14: 1 × Magnetic encoder NME2 (on the brake), for the external closed-loop controller (Nanotec)
encoder.why: Closes the loop for the stepper: the controller knows the motor angle and so the jaw position.

gearbox.title: Planetary gearbox
gearbox.what: pos. 18: 1 × Planetary gearbox GP42-S1-7-SR (Nanotec); pos. 3: 1 × Drive bracket (own part, milled, EN AW-6082 T6)
gearbox.why: Multiplies the small motor torque so the pinion reaches the grip force; the bracket holds the motor-brake stack beside it.
values: ratio i = 7.07, efficiency η = 0.9
319 g with the bracket

bevel.title: Spiral bevel pair
bevel.what: pos. 21: 1 × Spiral miter gear m = 1.5, z = 20, left hand, bore 8 H7 + key 2, hub turned to D16, faced to mounting dist. 19 (KHK SMSG1.5-20L, S45C, teeth induction hardened); pos. 22: 1 × Spiral miter gear m = 1.5, z = 20, right hand, bore 8 H7 + keyway 2 JS9 for the gearbox shaft key, M4 set screw, hub turned to D16 x 5 (KHK SMSG1.5-20R, S45C, teeth induction hardened)
bevel.why: Turns the drive by 90°: the motor lies flat along the housing instead of standing on top of it - a short gripper keeps the payload lever and the wrist torque small.
values: m = 1 pair (before 21 Nov) used 144 % of its allowed surface torque 0.97 N·m - too weak
built m = 1.5 pair: 40 % of 3.47 N·m
DIN 988 shim rings under the wheel hub set the mesh at assembly

pinion.title: Pinion shaft with bearings
pinion.what: pos. 8: 1 × Pinion shaft m = 1, z = 20 (own part, turned + hobbed, 16MnCr5 case hardened); pos. 13: 2 × Deep groove ball bearing 608-2Z (DIN 625 (Schaeffler / SKF), steel)
pinion.why: One pinion drives both racks. Fixed-loose bearing: the upper 608 is held by the two retaining rings, the lower one can slide, so heat and tolerances cannot jam the shaft.
values: m = 1.0, z = 20 → d = 20 mm; z = 20 lies above the undercut limit of 17 teeth
case-hardened 16MnCr5 teeth
pos. 37: 1 × Retaining ring DIN 471 8 x 0.8 (fixed bearing, shaft) (standard part, spring steel)
pos. 38: 1 × Retaining ring DIN 472 22 x 1 (fixed bearing, bore) (standard part, spring steel)
pos. 36: 1 × Parallel key DIN 6885 A 2 x 2 x 12 (bevel wheel) (standard part, C45+C)

racks.title: Racks
racks.what: pos. 19: 1 × Rack m = 1, 10 x 12, 14 teeth, cut to 44.0 (Maedler, C45); pos. 20: 1 × Rack m = 1, 10 x 12, 35 teeth, cut to 110.0 (Maedler, C45)
racks.why: Rack and pinion keep the jaws parallel and the force constant over the whole stroke; with one pinion between two racks the jaws always move together, so the part is centred.
values: m = 1, 10 × 12 mm (DIN 867 profile), screwed through ±1 mm slots along the stroke
stroke 10 mm per jaw: pads 86 mm apart when open, 70 mm part

rail.title: Ball rail and carriages
rail.what: pos. 15: 1 × Miniature ball rail size 12, L = 125, T1 = 12.5 (Bosch Rexroth R0445 203 31, steel); pos. 11: 2 × Ball carriage SLS size 12, long, preload (Bosch Rexroth R0444 213 01, steel)
rail.why: A preloaded ball rail guides both jaws without play and takes the moments of the jaw lever.
values: size 12: static load safety S0 5.1 - 7.8 (Rexroth asks 5 - 8; size 9 gave only 2.5 - 3.7) (rexroth_ksf_mini_R999001206.pdf p. 9)
C0 5630 N, Mt0 33.5 N·m, ML0 29.2 N·m per carriage (rexroth_ksf_mini_R999001206.pdf p. 19)
rail L = 125 mm, pitch 25 mm

slides.title: Slides
slides.what: pos. 10: 2 × Slide (own part, milled, EN AW-6082 T6)
slides.why: Connect carriage, rack and jaw holder on each side.
values: 2.5 mm wider than the carriage on each side, so the M3 counterbores keep a wall
81 g each

holders.title: Jaw holders and quick change
holders.what: pos. 7: 2 × Jaw holder (own part, milled, EN AW-6082 T6); pos. 35: 2 × Knurled thumb screw DIN 653 M5x20 (jaw retention, by hand) (standard part, steel); pos. 34: 4 × ISO 8734 4x12 (standard part, steel)
holders.why: Jaws can be changed by hand: two dowels locate the jaw, a knurled thumb screw from outside holds it against pulling off - no tool, no loose parts.
values: holder 10 / 14 mm thick above / below the cover, 38 mm wide (2 mm wall beside the screw counterbores)
to the slide: 2 × ISO 4762 M4x25 per side
the thumb screw replaced a spring plunger that sat in the wrong direction (review 23 Nov)

jaw.title: T-jaw
jaw.what: pos. 6: 2 × Jaw (own part, milled, EN AW-7075 T6)
jaw.why: The wide, low pad sits on the flat zone of part B. Its centre of mass is below the pads, so when the robot accelerates the part wants to twist; the wide pad gives the friction a long lever against that twist.
values: web 8 × 25 mm, 88 mm wide at the pad
FEM at full current (63.6 N): 8.4 MPa in the jaw, safety 54; pad tilt 0.059°
EN AW-7075 T6: high strength, light - the jaws move with every grip
54 g each

pad.title: Pad plate
pad.what: pos. 16: 2 × Pad plate, rubber-metal (steel 3 + NBR 70 Sh A 3) (bought to drawing, S235 / NBR)
pad.why: NBR is oil resistant and grips oily PA 6. Vertical grooves let the oil run off the contact face.
values: steel 3 mm + NBR 70 Shore A 3 mm, pad face 82 mm wide
grooves 1.5 mm wide, 1.0 mm deep, every 4 mm
design friction µ = 0.2 (oily part); µ = 0.3 expected with the grooves, to be measured
2 × ISO 4762 M3x6 from the back: the pad can be replaced

screws.title: Standard parts
screws.what: ISO 4762 socket head cap screws, ISO 10642 countersunk screws, ISO 8734 dowel pins, ISO 4029 set screws - all strength class 8.8 or better
screws.why: Only standard sizes M3 and M4 (M6 at the robot flange, M5 thumb screws), all off the shelf. Countersunk screws wherever a face must stay flat (cover, window, adapter); dowel pins wherever a part must come back to exactly the same place (racks, jaws, flange).
values: M3 for plates on 7 mm walls, M4 for the loaded joints (gearbox, hood, holders)
wire thread inserts where screws in aluminium are opened often (hood, top plate)
